origin: T33 hand-off (Ian team research, 2026-10-24); re-verified by T38

source.title: Case report: First diagnosis of Fabry disease in North Macedonia in a patient presenting with kidney failure on hemodialysis.

confirmation.summary: Hemizygous pathogenic GLA c.443G>A; near-absent GLA activity and raised Lyso-Gb3.
evidence: Genetic testing identified a known pathogenic GLA missense variant c.443G>A or p.(Ser148Asn) in the hemizygous state
almost undetectable GLA activity (0.1 μmol/L/h, normal: >2.8 μmol/L/h) and greatly elevated Lyso-Gb3

note.text: I've had burning pain in my arms and legs since I was young. I often get stomach cramps and struggle in both hot and cold weather. I hardly sweat at all. Over the last several years, doctors have told me my blood pressure was high and my kidneys were getting worse. I now need regular treatment to clean my blood, and tests have also shown problems with my urine and heart.
note.author: T33 hand-off (assistant-written from the article; not the patient's words)
